item.source_question_text:
Which of the following statements is correct?
A. We can assume a "spherical cow" when analyzing the motion of a cow's leg. [incorrect]
B. We can safely assume a cow is a point mass when analyzing its position change in the scale of a mile over a certain time period. [correct]
C. We can never assume the cow is in a vacuum, even when we need to ignore the effect of air resistance. [incorrect]
D. None of the above is correct. [incorrect]
item.generated_question_text:
Which statement best describes a reasonable physics approximation?
A. It is always acceptable to treat a human arm as a point particle when studying how the elbow joint rotates. This confuses rotational motion (where size/shape matters) with translation of the center of mass. [incorrect]
B. When tracking a hiker’s location on a map over several kilometers, modeling the hiker as a point mass is usually adequate. Over kilometer-scale motion the object’s size is negligible compared with the displacement, so a point-mass model is appropriate. [correct]
C. If you neglect air drag in a calculation, you are never allowed to describe the situation as “in vacuum.” This incorrectly treats “vacuum” as forbidden language rather than a modeling idealization used to ignore air effects. [incorrect]
D. None of the above is correct. Option B is a standard and valid approximation for large-scale position changes. [incorrect]

item.generated_question_text:

What is the ball’s speed at its maximum height (neglect air resistance)?
A. v0. This ignores that the vertical component of velocity decreases to zero at the top. [incorrect]

D. 0. Only the vertical component becomes zero at the top; the horizontal component generally remains nonzero. [incorrect]

C. It increases by a factor of 3. [correct]
D. It increases by a factor of 9. [incorrect]
